w: As part of Children's Day program, a drama 'Sowing the seeds of Satsang' showed how the 'Bal Basics Contest in Satsang' (BBC-S) program was set up. The BBC-S project, with the aid of a CD ROM and booklet was an effort to educate children with an in-depth knowledge of Satsang, its rituals and traditions. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly emphasizing the need to expose children to our culture and character. "If we fail to instil character in our children then it will be a blot and a source of misery for us. The belief that if children who will not roam or be exposed to outside things will be left behind and outdated is wrong. People feel that if children get involved in religious things then they will become passive - but this is not true! So it is important to inspire values and spirituality in them ..." Swamishri then presented prizes to groups of a total of 856 children who had successfully participated in the Bal Basics Contest Program.

Shri Vilasrao Deshmukh, Chief Minister of Maharashtra state, India, was highly impressed by his visit to the mandir and received the blessings of Swamishri. In his opinion about the mandir, he wrote, "I am fortunate to visit this temple - a monument of Hinduism and its concepts. This is one of the wonders of the recent history. Only dedicated people could have done this and Swamiji's blessings could bring this dream true. This is a pilgrimage outside India. I am glad to visit this and in getting the blessings of Swamiji. This will help unite humanity."

There were still about five minutes before the set time for going to the assembly. Pramukh Swami Maharaj asked for a writing pad. He asked for a letter, asked for a pen, and folding his right leg cross-legged on the bed, rested the pad on it and began to write. His left leg, hanging down, was also about three inches above the ground. In this position Swamishri wrote a letter filling about two large foolscap sheets.

Everyone bowed to Swamishri, who squeezes every moment of life into devotion to God. Just as Swamishri finished the letter, Atmaswarup Swami brought the certificate awarded to Swamishri by the "Guinness Book of World Records". Just as the London mandir has been honoured by this organisation as the largest stone-built Hindu mandir in the West, in the same way this organisation has also honoured Swamishri with a certificate for setting a record by building 355 mandirs in eleven countries of the world from 17 April 1971 to 2000. Its formal presentation is to be made at a ceremony in the coming days. The certificate was shown to Swamishri. Swamishri learnt the details and then, addressing two or three sadhus standing in front, said, "Look, brothers... this is all very well, but our record of saintliness is greater. Get going and break that..."
"There is no higher position than that of a sadhu." That ring echoed in Swamishri's words. And in his eyes, that has always remained the greatest record.

Swamishri performed his morning puja at the Akshardham site. Thereafter, the rituals for the first stone-laying ceremony of Akshardham monument commenced. Swamishri performed pujan, sprinkled sanctified water and panchamrut on the first sculpted stone. The murti of Harikrishna Maharaj was placed on the stone and arti was performed. Swamishri then offered pushpanjali and prayers for the early and unique construction of Akshardham. After the chanting of Janmangal paath, Swamishri showered rice grains and blessed the stones, sadhus and devotees. Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami performed the auspicious ritual of splitting the coconut on the first stone. Finally, Swamishri poured mortar under the first stone.

The gathering then transformed into an assembly. Pujya Viveksagar Swami , Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami and dignitaries elaborated upon the noble mission of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Swamishri, and the purpose of Akshardham monument. Swamishri buoyantly blessed the assembly.
In the evening, Swamishri arrived in Amdavad by flight from N. Delhi.
If you realise and internalize that you are atma then the sufferings of countless births will dissolve.
The goal of life is to realise that you are atma and have to offer bhakti to God. If you forget this goal then you have forgotten your roots.
When sufferings come, believe it to be God's wish. Contemplate on God's glory and samkhya vichar.
ph: Swamishri blesses the devotees and sadhus by showering rice grains

st.t: First Stone Laying Ceremony at Akshardham, New Delhi
w: With the divine blessings of Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj and the inspiration of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the construction of Akshardham in the lap of river Yamuna in New Delhi is proceeding at a tremendous pace.
On the auspicious day of Monday 2 July 2001, a significant landmark was ceremoniously celebrated - the first sculpted stone was placed in position by Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

Upon the sturdily built 20-feet deep foundations - capable of withstanding even major earthquakes - the construction has reached the plinth level - at a height of over 40 feet above ground level. Now the task of assembling the sculpted pink stones of Bansipahadpur in Rajasthan has begun.

A Vedic ceremony was performed from 9.00 - 10.00 am in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj to commemorate this auspicious occasion. Over 350 devotees witnessed this divine occasion, with Swamishri seated on the 40ft high plinth performing the Vedic rites.
Swamishri asked a young teenager called Kapil Dave, "How are you?"
Kapil replied, "I'm fine."
Then a sadhu said with humor, "He wakes up at 12 noon."

Swamishri advised, "You should not get up at 12 noon, but wake up in time, take your bath in time, play according to a scheduled time and perform bhajan, bhakti and listen to discourses too." Someone added, "Though he loves to eat outside (restaurant, etc.), he has taken a pledge not to do so."
Kapil clarified, "The pledge is for four months."

Swamishri said, "How can you pledge for four months only! You should not eat outside for life. It is the command of Yogiji Maharaj that one should not eat outside. Besides, you are a Brahmin's son and a satsangi. So, you should not eat from outside. From today stop eating outside."
Swamishri's instruction reflects his desire to stop the deterioration in a budding teenager's life - be it through irregular timings or laxity in niyams.

w: In the evening satsang assembly an impressive program was presented by children of 7 to 8 years (shishus). They presented a seminar on the supreme glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Gunatitanand Swami as Aksharbrahma, how Shastriji Maharaj established the knowledge of Akshar Purushottam and the Satpurush as the doorway to liberation. The satsangi children fluently recited references from Vachanamrut, Swamini Vato and Satsangijivan scriptures. The assembly of more than 12,000 devotees were amazed by the flawless presentation of children. Swamishri congratulated them for their excellent presentation.

Yuvak - Yuvati National Convention Delegates of the Yuvak-Yuvati National Convention started off their day by having darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj as he performed his morning puja in front of a beautiful replica of Sarangpur's Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir. Following this, sadhus spoke in great detail about both Swamishri's life message of doing good for others, as well as Bhagwan Swaminarayan's eternal message of attaining peace in this world and the next by following basic rules of conduct. Swamishri also blessed the morning assembly with his presence, playing a ‘Mukhpath’ game with the yuvaks.

Swamishri also visited the exhibition at the National Convention site, which included a replica of Gondal's Akshar Deri, a section with large-scale pictures of Swamishri's vicharan, and a section about important Hindu scriptures. In the evening session, the Guru Purnima festival was celebrated. Sadhus described how the true guru is the closest to God on earth, as God resides in every pore of his body. They also explained how true guru pujan is not merely physical reverence for the guru, but by abiding by his every desire.

Delegates of the Yuvak-Yuvati National Convention started off their day having darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj as he performed his morning pooja in front of a beautiful replica of Sarangpur's Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir.

Following this, saints spoke in great detail about both Swamishri's life message of doing good for others, as well as Bhagwan Swaminarayan's eternal message of attaining peace in this world and the next by following basic rules of conduct.
Swamishri also blessed the morning assembly with his presence, playing a "Mukhpaath" game with the yuvaks, providing them with memories to last a lifetime.

After lunch, Swamishri was counselling devotees. A youth approached, presented Swamishri with an invitation to his wedding and remarked. “I’m getting married. People will come and give me gifts. But what will you give me?”
“Blessings,” Swamishri replied, “may you have a happy married life and progress in satsang,”
“All that is fine,” the youth commented, “but will you give me Akshardham?”
“If you observe all the niyams and dharma of a householder, offer bhakti and service and have firm faith in Maharaj and Swami, then Maharaj will give you Akshardham.”
Saturday, 2 July 2005 (Jeth vad 11, Samvat 2061), Jamnagar

Bhavikbhai Panchasara is an NCC cadet. He had to go for an interview for training at the Indian Military Academy. Only five people from the whole country are selected for this interview. There are three interviews in the selection process. Bhavikbhai's first interview was in Rajkot. A colonel was conducting the interview. Seeing the tilak chandlo on Bhavikbhai's forehead, he said, "Wipe off the tilak chandlo."
"That will not be possible," Bhavik replied firmly. Then the colonel said, "I will let it pass in the first interview, but do not come to the second interview with tilak chandlo."

At the second interview the same colonel and a brigadier were sitting. Seeing Bhavik, the colonel and the brigadier said, "Your interview will be taken only if you remove the tilak chandlo." Then Bhavikbhai said, "I will never remove the tilak chandlo." Saying this, he was leaving the interview room when the brigadier called him back and said, "If you remove the tilak chandlo, you will be selected for the next camp and your life will be made. There are very good chances ahead. If you keep the tilak chandlo, you will suffer a great loss." Then Bhavikbhai told him plainly, "Keeping the tilak chandlo is itself a great gain for me. If you want to give me the job, give it; if not, thank you." Saying this he walked out of the room. He did not take the job at the cost of his tilak chandlo. For the sake of firmness in his vows, he gave up the chance of a good job.

Before this too he had gone to an NCC camp in Halol. After going there, he learnt that pure vegetarian food would not be available at this camp. So he had pickles and dry snacks sent from home, and for twelve days in a row he lived on these snacks and rotlis and kept his vow.
A youth came with his wedding invitation. He said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "It is my wedding. People will come and give gifts, but what will you give me?"
"Blessings. That your married life is happy and your satsang grows."
"That is all very well, but will you give me Akshardham?"
"If, living as a householder, you do seva and devotion according to your rules and dharma, and keep firm faith in Maharaj and Swami, then Maharaj will give you Akshardham."

During the meetings, Dr Satishbhai Tatamiya came for darshan. He has a pathology lab in the city. Yesterday the city's leading doctors had come, and he too had come for darshan with them. After a moment's darshan and blessings of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, when he went home he experienced divine changes in his mind and body, and felt as if his thoughts had come to a standstill. He could not sleep all night, so today he came to Swamishri. On his behalf his friend told Swamishri, "His thoughts have simply stopped! He cannot say what he is experiencing." Swamishri again placed his hand on his head and said, "He has become joyful at having found God. That bliss came, so his sleep at night went away." Saying this much, Swamishri gave him vartman and made him take refuge in Maharaj. He was blessed to experience the divinity of Swamishri's touch.
Saturday, 2 July 2005 (Vikram Samvat 2061, Jeth vad 11), Jamnagar

In any activity, especially when one is working with others, there is a likelihood of angry verbal exchanges arising. A maintenance volunteer expressed this problem to Swamishri, “While doing seva, sometimes, by telling the truth it is difficult to say it politely. I have to talk harshly.” Swamishri gave a solution, “While working together such things do happen, but on perceiving the glory (mahima) of the person concerned things would finally turn out well. Also, forget the incident immediately. Let it be like parting of water, which immediately returns to normal.”

A gutsy devotee asked, “Bapa, give me misery.” Swamishri replied, “There is no need to ask for pain and unhappiness. However, one should ask for happiness to the extent that one can worship God properly. It is fine to have misery to the degree that one never forgets God.”

A devotee was making efforts to acquire land for a mandir. The proprietors of the land were living abroad. Out of them two or three were heavy drinkers. They had refused to sell the land. The devotee informed Swamishri, “They are not ready to understand at all!” Swamishri encouraged him, “But keep trying.” The devotee quipped, “It seems that I’ll have to sit down with them to drink. Only then will they understand and agree.” Swamishri dissolved his proposal instantly, “No. There is no need to do that at all!” “Then you do something,” the devotee instantly appealed to Swamishri with the desire to reform them. Swamishri blessed, “Do bhajan and pray to God. By his grace they will agree to give the land.”
Emotional Relief

8 July 2008, Sarangpur A teenager broke down crying in repentance before Swamishri. He spoke choked with emotion, “Two or three years ago I had gone for darshan to one of our mandirs. There someone stole my slippers. Since then I started hating the mandir and pledged not to go at all. But I don’t know how I restarted going to the mandir.” The teenager broke down again. Then he added, “I cannot fix my mind on studies. I cannot concentrate.” Swamishri blessed and reassured him, “It is good that you have started going to the mandir. You’ll be able to pacify your mind. Shake off your depression. Go to the mandir regularly and pray to Maharaj.” The teenager left feeling relieved.
“I have God.”

11 July 2008, Sarangpur A disciple was returning from Dubai to India the next day. He rang up to ask whether Swamishri wanted anything. Swamishri replied, “I don’t want anything.” The attendant sadhu told Swamishri, “You are a sadhu. You want God.” Swamishri responded, “That I have. Where is the need to ask? I have God!”

ds.t: Ask for happiness in which God is worshipped
w: With reference to the line "Kuntaji dukh mang ke lino..." (Kunti asked for suffering), with the idea that in suffering God is worshipped, a devotee said joyfully to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "Bapa! Give me suffering."

Swamishri immediately said, "There is no need to ask for suffering, but ask for happiness of such a kind and such a measure that God is worshipped well. It is fine if there remains enough suffering that God is not forgotten."

ds.t: Ask for the happiness that helps you worship God
w: With reference to the line "Kuntaji dukh mang ke lino..." (Kunti asked for suffering), and with the feeling that in suffering one worships God, a devotee said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj in an exalted mood, "Bapa! Give me suffering."

Swamishri at once said, "There is no need to ask for suffering. Ask for as much happiness, and the kind of happiness, that lets you worship God well. It is fine if there is just enough suffering that God is not forgotten."

ds.t: Ask for happiness that helps worship God
w: With reference to the line "Kuntaji dukh mang ke lino..." (Kunti asked for suffering...), and with the feeling that in suffering one remembers God, a devotee said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj with fervour, "Bapa! Give me suffering."

Swamishri immediately said, "There is no need to ask for suffering, but ask for as much happiness, and such happiness, as lets you worship God well. It is fine to have just enough suffering that you do not forget God."

ds.t: Ask for happiness that lets you worship God
w: Referring to the line 'Kuntaji asked for sorrow...', with the feeling that in sorrow God is worshipped, a devotee said to Swamishri with fervour, "Bapa! Give me sorrow."

Swamishri said at once, "There is no need to ask for sorrow. Ask for as much happiness, and such happiness, that God can be worshipped well. It is fine to have just enough sorrow that God is not forgotten."

When Pramukh Swami Maharaj went up into the mandir, Maheshbhai Vaidya of Ahmedabad was holding a celebration with the ochhavia mandali (devotional singers) here, accompanied by the pakhavaj (drum). He was singing, "You look splendid as you come to Delhi, it has become very hot and humid, now send down the saffron rain." Hearing this meaningful request, Swamishri too looked at him and gave his consent, and after that a dhun (chant) for rain began.
After darshan, Swamishri came under the dome. At that time everyone was chanting the dhun, "Swaminarayan... Swaminarayan... send the rain." Swamishri suddenly said, "Now it will rain."

As if Swamishri's prophetic words had come true, since this morning there had been heavy rain for three or four hours in South Gujarat and right up to Central Gujarat as far as Anand, and in the evening it rained from Ahmedabad to North Gujarat and up to Abu, and at night in Saurashtra too.

Dilipbhai Dholakia, president of the Gujarati Samaj here, and Kishorsinh and other office bearers came for darshan. Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed them. They said, "For the last nine years we have not held anything like an election in the Samaj. The president is appointed only by selection."

Hearing this, Swamishri said, "That is very, very good. There will be progress through it. Otherwise in elections everyone's views differ and there is opposition, so unity does not remain and progress does not continue."

When Pramukh Swami Maharaj went up into the mandir, Maheshbhai Vaidya of Ahmedabad, with a pakhawaj (drum) and the local group of festival singers, was singing festival songs. He was singing, "You look so graceful coming to Delhi, it is so very hot, now send down a saffron rain." Hearing this meaningful request, Swamishri too glanced at him and gave his consent, and after that a dhun (chant) for rain began.
After darshan, Swamishri came into the dome. At that time everyone was chanting the dhun, "Swaminarayan... Swaminarayan... send rain." Swamishri suddenly said, "Now it will rain."

As if Swamishri's prophetic words had come true, from this morning heavy rain fell for three or four hours in South Gujarat and right up to Central Gujarat as far as Anand, and in the evening it rained from Ahmedabad through North Gujarat up to Abu, and at night in Saurashtra too.

Dilipbhai Dholakia, president of the Gujarati Samaj here, and Kishorsinh and other office bearers came for darshan. Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed them. They said, "For the last nine years we have had nothing like an election in the Samaj. The president is appointed by selection."

Hearing this, Swamishri said, "That is very, very good. There will be development through it. Otherwise, in an election, everyone's views differ and there is opposition, so unity does not remain and development does not happen."

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for his meal, he said to his attendant, Gunvatsaldas Swami, "I have drunk Ensure milk, so I am not hungry, but I am sitting down to eat only to please the devotees. So give me something that needs more chewing." Accordingly, Swamishri took paneer curry and kept the meal going for half an hour.
What affection for the devotees! Would the devotees know that Swamishri sometimes does even this for them!
